newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia plans merit system for insurance firms.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia plans merit system for insurance firms.

text.p: Malaysia will introduce a merit/demerit system to help insurance companies become more competitive, Bank Negara said in a statement on Thursday.

The system will, among others, use the number of complaints against each insurance company, said the statement, which was issued after the central bank's annual conference with chief executives and principal officers of insurance companies.
Other main factor to determine competitiveness under the system would be contribution of firms towards development and improvement of the industry.
The Bank Negara statement said it will also revise the ratio in which life insurance surpluses are distributed between policyholders and shareholders.
It said the ratio will be revised further in favour of policy holders, who get 80 percent of the surpluses at present.
Under the new system, the "proportion of surplus to policyholders will increase as the size of participating life fund increases", the central bank said.
It said that in the first six-months of the current year, the life insurance industry's new premium grew by just 0.1 percent versus 17.6 in the corresponding period last year.

"The slowdown in growth rate was partly attributable to the adjustments in the industry following implementation of the Guidelines on Operating Costs of Life Insurance Business" earlier this year, the statement said.

It quoted the Bank Negara Governor Ahmad Mohd Don, who is also Director General of Insurance, as saying that the planned merit system will complement the central bank's efforts to develop a core of large, well managed and disciplined insurers.
Malaysia has introduced a two-tier system in an effort to induce mergers and capital expansion among insurance companies before the country liberalises its markets further.
